svg.title: 09 · Data Architecture
svg.desc: Writer and reader services on the left connect to the stores they use. The central_ledger MySQL database holds participant, transfer, quote, settlement, reference and FX entities and is shared by central-ledger, central-settlement, quoting and the reporting API. mysql-als holds the account lookup and MSISDN oracle databases. MongoDB holds the object store, TTK and reporting databases. Redis holds caches and connector state; Kafka carries transient messages. Consistency rules and retention facts are on the right.
svg.text: Where data lives, who owns and writes it, the main entities, how data moves, and the consistency rules the ledger relies on
MySQL container mysql · 108 tables (verified) · schema owner: central-ledger migrations
FX quote and FX transfer tables (upstream migrations)
oracleEndpoint: which oracle serves which party ID type
party ID types; party data is relayed, not stored
central-ledger object store (bulk payloads; bulk unused here)
Audit events for the Finance Portal (optional profile)
Proxy cache for inter-scheme routing; rebuilt if lost
SDK in-flight transfer state; lost on failure
23 topics; message envelope id, from, to, type, content,
Writes quotes (not in simple routing mode)
Writes windows, settlements and MLNS transfers
Reads central_ledger with the central_ledger user
Each owns its own database (migrations at start)
ALS · ML API adapter · ledger · SDKs
Cache reads and writes; SDKs keep state in their own
One authoritative state per transfer: the latest transferStateChange row
Positions are double-entry: payer and payee changes sum to zero
No double processing: duplicate check on transferId + request hash
Ordering: position messages keyed per account; batch applied in one DB transaction
Both FSPs agree: ILP condition / fulfilment plus final notifications; GET /transfers/{id}
Settlement resets positions via the Hub multilateral account; FSP SETTLEMENT accounts
central-ledger, central-settlement, quoting and the reporting API share central_ledger. It
keeps the ledger consistent, but couples their releases and makes this one MySQL instance
Ledger, audit and Kafka retention: not configured
Encryption at rest: none; MongoDB and Redis without auth
Personal data: party names relayed by ALS, quote parties stored
FSP → API (FSPIOP JSON) → Kafka envelope → handlers → MySQL
Every service → topic-event-audit → events processor → MongoDB reporting → reporting API
Payee FSP → ALS → payer FSP (party data relayed, not stored)
Table names from the upstream migrations at the pinned tags, checked against the live databases on 2026-11-04. Target retention and backups: analysis/data-architecture.md §5.
